entries.condition: still_grid.png vs reference_a.png, landmark positions from metrics.json
entries.evidence: Horizon sits at y=0.222 (reference 0.25) and the plane centroid at (0.795,0.755) matches the reference (0.813,0.752), but the plane is nose-on to the camera instead of heading away upper-left, its wingspan is 0.231 of frame width against 0.1325, the main island spans the full frame width (green area 12.9% of frame vs 5.2% island area in the reference), the causeway starts at (0.711,0.530) instead of (0.395,0.475) and never crosses the island, and the skyline is split into two clusters (C3 and G3-H3) instead of one continuous band.
entries.defect: The camera framing is right but the scene content under it (aircraft heading, aircraft size, island extent, causeway origin, skyline layout) does not match the reference layout.
entries.fix: Rotate the initial aircraft pose to heading ~330 deg with 8-10 deg left bank, scale the aircraft down 1.75x in this view, shrink the main island to ~20% of frame width so open water shows on both sides, start the causeway from mid-island and run it through the island to the single skyline.

entries.condition: crops/aircraft.png at 324 px, plane viewed from front-above
entries.evidence: A high-wing, twin-float layout is recognisable, but the wing is a constant-chord slab with no taper, washout or dihedral, the fuselage reads as a short bulbous capsule because the nose points at the camera, and no vertical fin or stabiliser is visible behind it.
entries.defect: Wing planform and fuselage length do not read like a Beaver-class floatplane, and the pose hides the tail entirely.
entries.fix: Give the wing a tapered outer panel and 2-3 deg dihedral, lengthen the aft fuselage, and orient the plane so the fin and stabiliser contribute to the silhouette.

entries.condition: crops/aircraft.png and 3x zoom of the fuselage
entries.evidence: Float and wing struts are single-pixel hairlines that break into dashes, the engine cowl is a flat disc with a dot hub, the floats are smooth capsules with a yellow tip and one black bump each, and a small unlit yellow quad sits on the fuselage roof beside two white quads.
entries.defect: Struts are too thin to shade, the cowl has no cylinder/exhaust/prop detail, and light sprites render as flat quads on top of the body.
entries.fix: Model struts as 4-6 cm cylinders with fairings, add a cowl ring, exhaust stubs and a three-blade prop, and replace the quad markers with emissive geometry attached to the mesh.

entries.condition: yellow leading-edge extent measured in still.png
entries.evidence: Wingspan occupies 630 px of 1920 by bbox and 444 px by the yellow leading edge (0.231 of frame width) versus 0.1325 in the reference; the floats are longer than the nearest beach trees are tall at three times the distance.
entries.defect: The aircraft is about 1.75x too large for the reference camera and reads as a 25-30 m span machine.
entries.fix: Either move the aircraft 1.75x further from the camera in this view or correct the model scale so span is ~14.6 m relative to the 380 m camera altitude.

entries.condition: crops/aircraft.png, gloss and roughness read across body, wing and floats
entries.evidence: The navy fuselage shows one broad soft highlight and the same sheen on cowl, roof and belly, the wing is flat cream with a yellow stripe and four dark tick marks, and the floats show a single smooth gradient with no rivets, seams or scuffs.
entries.defect: Uniform roughness across the whole aircraft with no painted-metal micro-detail or dirt.
entries.fix: Author a PBR set with a roughness map (matte fabric-like wing paint vs semi-gloss cowl), panel-line normal map and weathering mask; add a clearcoat only on the fuselage.

entries.condition: crops/aircraft.png, windscreen and roof skylight area

entries.defect: Cockpit glass is opaque and indistinguishable from painted skin.
entries.fix: Use a transparent physical material (transmission ~0.9, IOR 1.5, low roughness) with a visible cabin interior and pilot behind it.

entries.evidence: Buildings are pastel extruded boxes (pink, yellow, grey) with flat roofs, no window texture, no setbacks and only a few needle spikes; a second city of the same boxes sits at the causeway end at G3-H3 where the reference shows open water.

entries.fix: Build the skyline from varied facade-textured meshes with rooftop plant, merge the two clusters into one band from A3 to G3 and remove the box city at the causeway end.

entries.condition: crops/environment.png and 3x shore zoom, colour measured with measure.py
entries.evidence: Island vegetation base measures (107,156,124) versus (58,63,64) in the reference, so it is 2.2x brighter and lime-green; the beach is a bluish white (173,199,213) band of nearly constant width that outlines the entire island like a stroke; the coastline is a smooth blobby polygon with no sandbars, mudflats or the reference's mangrove edge.
entries.defect: Flat lime grass plane with a uniform outline beach instead of varied dark canopy, sandbars and irregular shore.
entries.fix: Darken and vary the ground albedo, drive beach width from a noise-perturbed distance field, and add shallow sandbar and mudflat patches near the shore.

entries.condition: colour measured in still.png at three depths
entries.evidence: Near water is a saturated cyan (40,154,186, saturation 0.78) with a few dark blotches, far water fades to (141,186,209); the reference goes from teal-green shallows over visible sand to deep blue.
entries.defect: One saturated cyan tint with no bathymetry-driven colour change or visible bottom in shallows.
entries.fix: Blend water colour by depth (absorption + scattering) with a sand-bottom term in the first 5 m and desaturate the deep colour toward (60,120,170).

entries.condition: near water under the aircraft and along the shore
entries.evidence: No sky, cloud, aircraft or shoreline reflection is visible anywhere on the water; the surface is a diffuse colour field.
entries.defect: Reflections are missing entirely.
entries.fix: Add a planar or screen-space reflection with Fresnel falloff and a normal-mapped surface so the sky and the aircraft appear in the water.

entries.evidence: Three boats are visible (a white sail at D4, two dark hulls near the right city) and none has a wake; the shoreline foam is a uniform white band of constant width around the whole island with a few blocky speckles.

entries.fix: Add a V-wake mesh/particle trail scaled with boat speed and break the shore foam into wave-driven strips with varying width and gaps.

entries.evidence: Trees are two or three low-poly canopy meshes (round lollipop, layered blob, palm) at one size and one lime green, scattered at uniform density over flat grass, with no undergrowth, shrubs, shadows or dense stands.

entries.fix: Add 6-8 tree variants with random scale 0.7-1.3, darker canopy tones, clumping via noise, and ground shadows.

entries.evidence: The causeway is a thin flat ribbon from the island's east tip (0.711,0.530) to the right city (0.879,0.350) with no visible piers, railings or traffic and a double-loop arch at the far end; no road, marina approach or highway exists on the island, whereas the reference shows a highway with cars crossing the island and a piered causeway with an arch mid-span.

entries.fix: Route the causeway through mid-island with an approach road, add pier rows and a cable/arch span at the reference position, and generate island roads with traffic.

entries.evidence: Clouds are flat grey smears with no lit tops or shaded bases; only 7.5% of sky pixels are darker than the background versus 39% cloud cover with volumetric cumulus in the reference.
entries.defect: No cloud volume, just a grey noise layer.
entries.fix: Add volumetric or layered billboard cumulus with sun-lit tops, shaded bases and towering shapes over the bay.

entries.condition: sky and horizon colour measured in still.png and crops/distant.png
entries.evidence: Sky top measures (183,195,207) versus (69,141,179) in the reference, so the whole sky is milky white with no blue; the land horizon at y~0.24 is a razor-straight boundary between a flat green plane and the grey sky.
entries.defect: Uniform haze washes out the sky and a hard horizon seam replaces the graded haze.
entries.fix: Use a physically based sky with a blue zenith, limit haze to a height-fogged horizon band, and blend the far terrain into the sky colour.

entries.condition: shading on the aircraft and island in still_grid.png
entries.evidence: The aircraft has no readable light direction (wing top, fuselage side and floats are equally lit), the island shows no tree shadows, and exposure is split: sky luminance averages 194 while near water is 123.
entries.defect: Flat, direction-less lighting with over-exposed sky and no sun-lit/shadow contrast.
entries.fix: Set the sun high from behind-left of the camera per the reference, enable directional shadows, and tone-map with a lower exposure so the sky keeps colour.

entries.condition: island ground around trees and houses
entries.evidence: No tree, house, dock or aircraft shadows exist; the only darker patches on the grass are pale grey blotches that do not align with any object.
entries.defect: Shadows are absent.
entries.fix: Enable cascaded shadow maps for the directional light and bake or contact-shadow the tree bases.

entries.evidence: No sun glitter or specular streak exists on the water and the fuselage shows one broad soft highlight with no sharp specular.

entries.fix: Add a normal-mapped water surface with a GGX sun highlight and use a lower roughness on the fuselage clearcoat.

entries.evidence: Palette is candy cyan water, lime land and blue-white sand/haze; the reference is teal water, dark olive canopy, warm grey sand and a saturated blue sky.
entries.defect: Global blue-white cast with inverted saturation (water too saturated, sky too flat).
entries.fix: Apply a grade that warms sand and shadows, deepens the sky, desaturates water by ~30% and darkens vegetation.

entries.condition: still.png vs flight.png (3 s apart), patch tracking on 184 canopy samples
entries.evidence: 135 of 184 tree patches show zero whole-canopy displacement with local pixel change (mean residual 5.0), so sway is local rather than synchronised; foam and near water animate (5.4% of near-water pixels change), clouds and city are static; no popping or LOD swap is visible between the two frames.
entries.defect: No temporal defect visible at 3 s spacing, but the sway is too subtle to read as wind and cloud drift is absent.
entries.fix: Add gust-driven canopy sway with per-tree phase and slow cloud advection; keep the LOD stability.

entries.fix: Spawn on heading ~330 deg with a slight left bank so the plane flies into the scene, and populate telemetry in the frozen frame.

entries.condition: sky in the view labelled cloudy
entries.evidence: The sky is a single flat grey gradient with no individual cloud shapes, bases, breaks or layering.
entries.defect: Cloud volume is missing in the cloudy view.
entries.fix: Add a stratocumulus layer with visible cell structure, darker bases and thin breaks.

entries.evidence: Opaque navy windscreen/roof with no interior.
entries.defect: Opaque glass.
entries.fix: Transmissive glass with interior.

entries.evidence: The water stays saturated cyan with no grey sky reflection.
entries.defect: Reflections are missing; the water ignores the overcast sky.
entries.fix: Reflect the sky colour into the water with Fresnel weighting.

entries.evidence: Every island has a pale rim of constant width and no boats or wakes are present.
entries.defect: Uniform shore ring and missing wakes.
entries.fix: Vary the shallow rim with wave-driven foam and add boats.

entries.evidence: No sheen from the bright overcast sky on the water; the aircraft has one broad highlight.
entries.defect: Specular response is missing.
entries.fix: Add environment lighting from the sky and a rough specular on the water.

entries.evidence: A yellow quad floats above the cabin at E4, the fin is a thin plane and struts are 1-px lines.
entries.defect: Floating light quad and paper-thin parts.
entries.fix: Attach emissive nav lights to the mesh and thicken fin and struts.

worst3: A cloudy view with no clouds: flat grey gradient sky (A1-H2)
Saturated cyan water that ignores the overcast sky, with uniform pale island rims
Floating yellow quad above the cabin and opaque cabin glass (E4-E5)
best3: Dense dark canopy clusters on the islands read as real vegetation (A4-H5)
Far shore at A3-H3 dissolves softly into the grey haze
Layered islands at different distances give convincing depth

entries.evidence: Only a red beacon and a white light dot mark the aircraft; no wing, fuselage or float edge is visible.
entries.defect: Aircraft silhouette is invisible.
entries.fix: Add moonlight/ambient, a landing-light beam and cabin glow so the airframe reads at night.

entries.evidence: Surfaces do not pick up any city or sky light; the body renders black.
entries.defect: Materials show no response to environment light.
entries.fix: Add an environment map and ambient term so painted metal shows a faint sheen.

entries.evidence: No instrument or cabin glow is visible and the windscreen shows nothing.
entries.defect: Cockpit glass and interior lighting are absent.
entries.fix: Add a dim panel glow behind transmissive glass.

entries.evidence: Thousands of city light points at C3-H4 produce no streaks or reflection on the water.
entries.defect: Reflections are missing.
entries.fix: Reflect emissive lights on the water with roughness-stretched streaks.

entries.evidence: No boats, wakes or any surface disturbance; the water is a black grain field.
entries.defect: Water interaction is missing.
entries.fix: Add lit boats with wakes and a faint wave normal map.

entries.evidence: No moon glitter or sheen on the water and no highlight on the aircraft.
entries.defect: Specular response is absent.
entries.fix: Add a moon light with a water highlight and environment lighting.

worst3: Aircraft invisible except two light sprites: no ambient, landing light or cabin glow
City lights with no reflection on a black grain-filled water plane
Exposure so low that water, land and clouds are indistinguishable
best3: City light field has a plausible density gradient toward the core (D3-G3)
Bright cluster at H4 reads as a lit district
HUD remains legible against the dark frame
